SddReconcile.keywords: reconcile, fix, sync-from-code, drift, spec-probe, bug-vs-spec-defect, problem-class, blast-radius, back-sync, sdd-reconcile
SddReconcile.Mission:
Restore the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle after it desynced, then verify. A separate door (`/sdd-reconcile`). Two auto-detected modes converge on the same tail: - **fix** — a finding / bug / review drove it: the spec is (presumed) right, the code is wrong. - **from-code** — freeform code ran ahead of the spec: the code is the new reality, the spec is stale.
The heart is not the patch — it is the probe (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`): is this a bug or a spec-defect, what is the problem's class, what is the blast radius. Both modes end with the SAME tail: back-sync specs / tasks, then verify. Patching the symptom alone is not SDD.
Input — findings / a bug / a review, OR "I changed code, formalize it". Output — code and/or spec moved to agreement, tasks reopened / created, trackers synced, gates green.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive text (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact text and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any of its worktrees), invoke them repo-relative from the working tree's own root — `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts ` — never a hardcoded path to a different checkout; this is rewritten to `npx gennady ` by the path-normalizer when the directives are synced into a project. In every OTHER project, invoke the published package: `npx gennady `. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Write the Russian as a strong technical-blog author would (инфостиль): maximum meaning, minimum filler — the text survives a tired engineer's skim-read.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms. - Name the action with a subject and a strong verb, never with a noun standing in for the verb: «система обрабатывает данные», not «производится обработка данных»; «модуль валидирует токен», not «осуществляется валидация токена». Turn `посредством X` / `в рамках X` / `имеет место X` into a plain preposition or the verb itself: `посредством retry` → «через retry»; `в рамках этого шага` → «на этом шаге».
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
- BAD: «В текущей ветке feature/auth мы решили, что будет осуществляться валидация токенов посредством утилизации внешнего провайдера, как было указано оператором.» - GOOD: «Модуль валидирует токены через внешнего провайдера.» - Fixes: drops the session leak («текущая ветка feature/auth», «как было указано оператором» — per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`); replaces the bureaucratic noun-verb («осуществляется валидация») with subject+strong verb; drops the calque («утилизация» for «использование»).

Move forward unless stopped — gated by confidence and stakes: - HIGH confidence + low-stakes step → show the result and proceed; the operator can object at any moment. - LOW confidence, OR a high-stakes step (architecture, pivot, a trust boundary, an irreversible choice) → hard stop, wait for the operator.
The agent never closes a step it is unsure about, and never auto-agrees to a risky shortcut (see `AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`).
Named hard stops — Approval Checks and the SCALE confirmation exchange — are exempt from the proceed rule; they always stop, however high the confidence.
Keep the dialogue compact: no repeat questions; group obvious questions into one; on long dialogues show the delta, not a full restate. Confidence is `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` and lives in the dim service line, not narrated each round.

The agent's job is to protect the operator from their own blind spots and lead them to a sound decision — even a junior operator. - Warn, don't only ask: name the risk that will hurt later, the requirement likely missing, the thing probably forgotten, the trust boundary (auth, payments, persistence) that needs a real runtime. - Pull the thread, don't fill a quota: after each answer, check whether it opened a new gap or risk; if so, follow it until the gap is actually closed — not until a question count is hit. - Ask developing questions — ones that deepen the topic and check what should and should NOT exist — not merely uncomfortable ones. Never announce a question; just ask it plainly. - Neutral and critical: if the operator wants to skip something risky, surface the cost and ask for a reason; never silently agree.
Blind-spot instincts (not a checklist to recite): canonical source of truth? behavior on dependency failure? where simulation ends and real runtime begins? who validates input here? which assumption, if wrong, kills the design?

Any reported problem, bug, or freeform change is first a question about the spec, not a line to patch. Before reconciling, establish three things against the spec: - **Bug or spec-defect?** Does the code violate a correct spec (→ fix the code), or is the code right and the spec was wrong (→ fix the spec and cascade downstream)? This decides which corner of the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle moves. - **The class.** Judging by the spec + this problem, where else does the same class occur? One report is a symptom — scan the closed-world inventory / contracts for siblings (`orient`). - **The blast radius.** From the diff, what else did the change touch that must be re-examined?
Patch only the symptom and you have not done SDD — the spec mediates everything, so reconcile at the right level and propagate.

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

Every fix routes through the task that owns the affected file — ownership is resolved from the artifacts, before classification. `@tasks: -[, ...]` in a file header names the owning task(s). Files matching `*.task.-.md` (co-located under `specs/`) are tickets — the Task-ID is in the filename. Files matching `*.1-spec.md` / `*.spec.md` are spec files — linked to a scope, not a single task. Index files (`*.2-tasks.md` / `*.3-tasks.md`, `specs/2-tasks.md` / `specs/3-tasks.md`) are global artifacts, owned by no task. The resulting file → [Task-IDs] map is what routes fixes per `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`.

A reported symptom is an entry point, never the class. Every finding MUST be classified BEFORE any edit: bug vs spec-defect, action category (direct-fix / spec-update / task-reopen), the full problem class and the blast radius. Triviality of a fix is confirmed by the blast-radius probe, never by self-assessment. A fix applied without this classification is a symptom patch, not SDD.
Multiple scattered changes with one shared intent (a mass rename, a parameter added across call sites) MUST be grouped into a single logical task. Per-item entries are noise.

Every finding is routed to the artifact that owns the remediation:
| Finding type | Action | |---|---| | `CLOSED_WORLD_DRIFT` | spec edit (add entity to Inventory) OR ticket reopen | | `COMPLETENESS_GAP` | ticket reopen — new Round N | | `RUNTIME_BACKING_VIOLATION` | spec edit (Deferred Runtime Scope) OR ticket reopen | | `RULES_COMPLIANCE_VIOLATION` | ticket reopen, new Round N | | `RULES_CASCADE_MISMATCH` | ticket update (per-phase `Rules:` list) | | `BDD_COVERAGE_MISMATCH` | ticket reopen OR ticket update (canonical case names) | | `EXECUTION_LOG_INCOMPLETE` | ticket update / reopen | | `INSIGHT_BACKFLOW` | spec edit (scope or module spec) | | `STALE_AFTER_PIVOT` | reopen / refine the affected downstream artifact | | `TASK_ID_DRIFT` | code-fix via ticket reopen | | `ENVIRONMENT_GATE_UNAVAILABLE` | operator escalation — NOT a phase fix and NOT something audit or the worker repairs itself; spin out as a separate infra/environment task if the fix is non-trivial | | `DEAD_CODE_SUSPECT` (spotted incidentally during a probe) | spin out as a separate task (background task / new ticket) — never fixed inside the current task; keeps the current blast radius bounded | | operator-acknowledged risk | Decision Log entry in the scope spec |
The audit agent proposes a concrete edit (diff or instruction). The operator decides and applies. The audit agent does not modify code autonomously (per `AX_NO_AUTO_FIX`).

Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.

In `pivot` mode every replaced decision: the old D-NNN → `status: superseded`. The new D-NNN carries `Was → Now` + `Supersedes: D-NNN` + a git ref pointing to the pre-rework state. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.

Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).

Phases within one ticket dispatch strictly sequentially, in the order declared by each phase's `Deps` — a phase starts only after every phase it depends on reaches `[x] DONE` in the current Round. Never dispatch two phases of the same ticket concurrently, even when their Target Files are disjoint and no `Deps` edge exists between them: Handoff threads linearly (`AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`) — phase N's Inputs are phase N-1's Handoff, so a phase dispatched before that Handoff exists has nothing to read.
Parallelism, where available, is only across separate tickets whose Target-File sets are disjoint (`AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`) — never within one ticket's own phases.

After all reopens are prepared, dispatch the reopened tasks through execute as one BATCH. The batch orchestrator will plan layers, run phases, close rounds, sync trackers.
Audit flag: pass `skip-audit` to the batch — per-task audit is skipped; the reconcile-level safety net (verify + fresh-eyes epic audit + code-review) runs ONCE at STEP_7 instead. (The batch still runs phases but skips the per-task audit dispatch.)
End every phase block with a typed Handoff line consumed by the next phase and the orchestrator. Format per `HANDOFF_FORMAT`. Free-form text forbidden — the next phase reads keys, not narrative.

When reopening a task ticket, append to Execution Log:
``` ### Round N — , fix:
| Phase | Kind | Status | Target Files | Deps | |-------|-------|--------|-------------|------| | P1 | fix | [ ] | | — | ```
Set ticket Meta Status → `[ ] TODO`. Update `Reopens: `. Sync tracker: `tasks//README.md` row → `[ ] TODO`, `tasks/README.md` index → adjust counts.
After all tasks complete, run sdd-check. All checks must PASS. If sdd-check finds issues → classify them as new findings → ask operator → fix cycle repeats.

SddReconcile.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INPUT` | Neither findings / bug nor a code change to reconcile | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Cannot tell fix from from-code — ask the operator | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the reconcile plan | | `H_TRIVIALITY_UNCONFIRMED` | Fix looks trivial but the probe leaves doubt, OR no critic was dispatched (a self-probe does not confirm triviality) — ask the operator: short-circuit or full path | | `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL` | Gates still fail after the reconcile |

Step.Action: Findings / bug / review present → `fix`. Code already changed / "formalize what I coded" / drift → `from-code` (`AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`; ambiguous → `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE`).

Intent-search the specs for the area in play + read the git diff; map which specs / tasks own it (`orient` for the entity / contract surface, `sdd-check` for the link / tracker state). This is the bounded read — not the whole repo.

Step.Goal: Probe the spec against the problem — the critical step (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`).
Step.Action: Dispatch the critic on the affected spec, seeded with the problem, to judge: **bug or spec-defect** (code violates a right spec, or the spec was wrong); **the class** (where else the same class occurs, via `orient` over the closed-world); **the blast radius** (what else the diff touches). MUST cover the full problem class and blast radius — the reported symptom is only the entry point. The critic MUST be an actually dispatched subagent — an orchestrator self-probe never satisfies this step and never confirms triviality, no matter how small the fix looks (mirrors `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`: triviality is confirmed by the probe, never by self-assessment). No dispatched verdict → `H_TRIVIALITY_UNCONFIRMED`. The probe verdict feeds STEP_2B.

Step.Goal: Resolve ownership, classify every finding — BEFORE any edit (`AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`).
Step.Action:
Build the ownership map first (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION`): per finding located in a `.ts` / `.spec.md` file — read the file header (first lines before `import` / first `#`), extract `@tasks: -[, ...]`, build file → [Task-IDs]. Header absent → classify anyway (the fix IS adding the header), note "no task" for the plan.
Classify each finding into an action category: - **direct-fix** — global / non-code artifact: tracker desync, execution-log placeholder, a missing header with no other findings. Edit the file directly, verify. - **spec-update** — spec gap: missing inventory entity, DbC contract gap, Decision Log gap, stale pivot artifact. Edit the spec; a spec change that invalidates code escalates to task-reopen. - **task-reopen** — ANY finding in a code file carrying `@tasks:`: bug, contract violation, missing test, BDD mismatch, review finding. Reopen the owning task per `AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`; pair every code-fix phase with a `test` phase (regression); multiple findings of one task go into a single reopen Round.
- WHEN the class is trivial: a single site, blast radius confirmed empty by the dispatched critic's verdict, contracts / specs untouched -> patch the code TOGETHER WITH a regression test covering the fixed case in the same run (a task-reopen always pairs code-fix with a `test` phase — the trivial branch is not exempt from that pairing just because it skips the Round), back-sync the spec (`sdd-sync`), run the light gate (typecheck + tests of the touched files, including the new regression test). - WHEN the light gate is green -> present `FIX_SUMMARY_FORMAT`. DONE — the full tail (STEP_3–7, epic audit + code-review) stays skipped. - WHEN the light gate is red AND the failure reproduces on the pre-change baseline AND lies outside the blast radius confirmed by the critic -> record it in `FIX_SUMMARY_FORMAT` as pre-existing (not caused by this patch), propose a separate task to the operator for it, and do NOT head the summary with "✅ complete" — the gate is still red. DONE. - OTHERWISE (the failure is caused by or overlaps the patch/blast radius) -> `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`. - WHEN triviality is plausible but the probe leaves doubt -> `H_TRIVIALITY_UNCONFIRMED` - DEFAULT -> STEP_3_PLAN, the full path

From the probe + STEP_2B categories, decide per item what moves: code → spec (fix the code via execution) or spec → code (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION` + cascade downstream) or both; reopen / create the affected tasks (`AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`), including the class siblings; group scattered edits sharing one intent into a single task (`AX_GROUPING_REDUCES_NOISE`) — per-finding tasks are noise; reconcile any new entity via `orient` (`AX_REUSE_FIRST`), filling the "Reuse rationale" slot for anything that lands on JUSTIFY. If STEP_2B found a file with a missing header, the plan MUST carry an explicit line to add it — the fix IS adding the header; this is not deferred to `sdd-sync`, which does not write headers. Present the plan (`PLAN_TABLE_FORMAT`).
Ask via `QUESTION_FORMAT`; warn about the class / blast the operator may not have seen (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`). Rejected → `H_OPERATOR_REJECT`. STOP.

Apply spec edits (defect / from-code); reopen / create tasks per the STEP_2B ownership map (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION`); dispatch the reopened tasks through execute as a BATCH with per-task audit skipped (`AX_DISPATCH_VIA_BATCH`; the dispatched workers stay spec-bound per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`) — one reconcile-level verify runs at STEP_7 instead (`AX_EXECUTION_ORDER`, `AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`, route per `AX_FINDING_ROUTING`).
`sdd-sync` brings specs / tasks / trackers into agreement with the final code. This tail is the same whether we entered as fix or from-code.

This full tail applies to the DEFAULT (non-trivial) path only — the trivial fix class already exited at STEP_2B with its own light gate (typecheck + tests of the touched files). Reaching STEP_7 means the path is non-trivial: run this full tail once here, never as an extra "to be safe" pass layered on top of an already-closed trivial path.
`sdd-check` + `sdd-verify --profile full` must pass (else `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`). Then — because per-task audit was skipped in the batch (`AX_DISPATCH_VIA_BATCH`) — restore the safety net ONCE at the reconcile level: dispatch a fresh-eyes epic audit (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/audit.directive.xml")`, per-epic — drift code↔spec over the reconciled set) and a code-review (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/code-review.directive.xml")` — bugs in the reconciled diff). A `BLOCKER` from either MUST pause and surface to the operator. Present the reconcile summary (`FIX_SUMMARY_FORMAT`).

ChatOutput.Contract:
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch) `` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👨‍💻` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.

Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### 💡 Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
### 💡 Стратегия миграции v1→v2 Три пути дают разный профиль риска и времени простоя, и откат стоит по-разному в каждом. - **Big-bang** `[migrate-all]` — _за: один переход, нет промежуточного состояния · против: долгий простой, откат дорогой_ - **Постепенная миграция по скоупам** `[migrate-incremental]` — _за: откат дешёвый, риск размазан во времени · против: два формата сосуществуют дольше_ - **Parallel-run с shadow-чтением** `[migrate-shadow]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск отката почти полностью ценой временной инфраструктуры
(AskUserQuestion: «Big-bang» · «Постепенная миграция» · «Parallel-run (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
### 💡 Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)

Shown to operator at STEP_3. Compact table per category. Operator may edit. Carries a "Reuse rationale" column/slot — filled per `AX_REUSE_FIRST` whenever an item introduces a new entity/type/method/contract: the JUSTIFY-level one-line rationale for why the existing surface was insufficient (reuse/extend items leave it empty — nothing to justify).

``` ## ✅ sdd-fix complete
Trivial fixes: N applied ✅ (+ regression test) →
Direct fixes: N applied ✅ → ✅ →
Spec updates: N applied ✅ →
Tasks reopened: N 🔄 TSK-NN — Round N: → dispatched 🔄 TSK-MM — Round N: → dispatched
🔍 sdd-check: ✅ PASS (N/N checks) ``` Omit any section whose count is 0. Every file changed on disk MUST appear under exactly one section — a summary whose counts are all zero while the diff is non-empty is a defective summary.
